data.text:
ICYMI O/N & WEEKEND

TARIFFS:

A divided U.S. appeals court ruled on Friday that most of Trump's tariffs (those justified under IEEPA, which include the "reciprocal" tariffs) are illegal. The court allowed the tariffs to remain in place through October 14 to give the Trump administration a chance to file an appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court. (RTRS)

Trump predicts a reversal of the decision, saying he expected tariffs to benefit the country "with the help of the Supreme Court." (Truth Social)

The Trump administration is continuing its talks with trading partners despite a U.S. appeals court ruling that most of President Donald Trump's tariffs are illegal, USTR Jamieson Greer said on Sunday. (Fox News)

Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday night, "More than 15 Trillion Dollars will be invested in the USA, a RECORD. Much of this investment is because of Tariffs. If a Radical Left Court is allowed to terminate these Tariffs, almost all of this investment, and much more, will be immediately cancelled! In many ways, we would become a Third World Nation, with no hope of GREATNESS again..."

MACRO:

The Federal Reserve announced on Friday that it had finalized new capital levels of the nation's largest banks following the June stress tests to take effect on October 1st, although it added that Morgan Stanley is seeking reconsideration of its upcoming capital level. (RTRS)

Economists project about 75,000 jobs were added in the US in August, based on the median of a Bloomberg survey, while the jobless rate is seen at 4.3%. Four straight months of sub-100,000 payrolls growth would mark the weakest such stretch since the onset of the pandemic in 2020. (BBG)

US Corporate Leverage Poised to Rise With  $1 Trillion Deals Deluge. (BBG) 

Investors underestimate Donald Trump’s threat to the Federal Reserve, economists warn. (FT)

Trump said on Saturday that he will issue an executive order to require voter identification from every voter. (RTRS)

A Trump administration request that Japan buy more U.S. rice caused this week's snag in bilateral trade talks as Tokyo "strongly objected" to the condition. (Nikkei)

U.S. tariffs took a toll on factory activity across Asia, overshadowing a surprisingly upbeat performance in China, private surveys showed on Monday. (RTRS)

Japan's government spending requests for next fiscal year will likely set a record for the third consecutive year, a draft of the requests obtained by Reuters showed on Monday, highlighting the challenge the country faces in fixing its dire finances. (RTRS)

Japanese corporate spending on plant and equipment climbed 7.6% in April-June from a year earlier, but the outlook for business investment has clouded as manufacturers' profits slide on pain caused by U.S. tariffs. (RTRS)

Hedge funds are starting to bet the yen is poised to snap out of its narrow trading range and march higher against the dollar. Leveraged investors are building positions in the options market that will benefit if Japan’s currency breaks free from its current narrow band of around 147 to the greenback and appreciate beyond 145, CME data showed. (BBG)

China’s official manufacturing gauge edged up in August but remained in contraction for a fifth straight month, as factory output picked up while market demand stayed subdued. PMI rose to 49.4 from 49.3, beneath expected 49.5. (WSJ)

A private gauge of China’s manufacturing activity jumped back into expansionary territory in August, rising to a five-month high. The RatingDog China PMI rose to 50.5 last month from 49.5 in July, according to data released Monday by S&P Global. (WSJ)

Hedge Funds Boost Options Bets for Yuan to Strengthen Past 7. (BBG)

China’s mega banks are under pressure from rising allowances for loan losses and a continued margin erosion in their mission to support the world’s second largest economy. (BBG)

President Xi Jinping said his country will increase investments and loans to partners while outlining a plan to bolster a China- and Russia-led security bloc and boost Beijing’s global clout. (BBG)

China's resale home prices fell again in August even as new-home prices edged up, underscoring persistent weakness in the crisis-hit property market despite a raft of support measures, a private survey (China Index Academy) showed on Monday. (RTRS)

'China Ups Surveillance of Troubled People to Quell Rising Unrest' WSJ article notes  Communist Party’s new ‘society work’ agency helps with emotional and economic setbacks while monitoring dissatisfied people. (WSJ)

China’s stock rally is set to get a boost from small investors, stoking hopes that their massive savings will fuel the next leg of the market’s blistering advance. (BBG)

China’s Stock Rally Is Met With Skepticism in Options Market. (BBG)

Australian job advertisements were steady in August, highlighting a still resilient labour market amid lower interest rates, while a bounce in retail hiring was expected to persist into coming months. (BBG)

Australian home prices rose in August, driven by increased buyer demand and low levels of advertised stock, property consultant Cotality said on Monday. (RTRS)

New Zealand home-building approvals remain in a slumber that extends back more than a year, adding to signs that weakness in the key construction industry may persist. (BBG)

New Zealand expects to appoint a new Reserve Bank governor within weeks, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said. (BBG)

Overseas-based investors with a New Zealand investor residence visa will be allowed to buy a house, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said on Monday. (RTRS)

ECB's Lagarde said the Federal Reserve losing its independence would pose a “serious danger” to the world, but But Lagarde told Radio Classique in an interview on Monday that President Trump would find it “very difficult” to take control of the US central bank, citing legal precedents that prevent the removal of Fed governors. (BBG)

Current uncertainty over inflation developments calls for “flexibility” in policy-making, European Central Bank Governing Council member Olli Rehn told Finnish newspaper Helsingin Sanomat. (BBG)

Germany has filled its gas reserves to a critical storage level two months ahead of schedule, easing fears about winter heating shortages that only recently fueled talk of potential government intervention. (BBG)

French Prime Minister Francois Bayrou struck a combative tone in his effort to gain support for a Sept. 8 confidence vote, while acknowledging that talks with political parties may fail to save his government from being ousted. (BBG)

Workers at Electricite de France SA plan to hold a three-day strike, adding to union calls for labor actions and deepening the political crisis in the country. (BBG)

French business warns of recession risk as political turmoil deepens. (FT)

Austria's next central bank chief Martin Kocher, who will take office on Monday, said in an interview on Saturday he does not see himself as a hawk or a dove but will ensure price stability is central to all European Central Bank decisions. (RTRS)

Kemi Badenoch has committed the Tories to extract as much oil and gas as possible from the North Sea. (BBG)

Home listings in the UK have been piling up for about a year — their longest streak in two decades — as cautious buyers and the rise in supply point to further downward pressure on prices, according to the latest Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors survey. (BBG)

India rebutted mounting US pressure to end crude imports from Russia, with Oil Minister Hardeep Puri arguing that the flows had helped to shield the global economy from a price spike, while also directly challenging blunt language used by White House adviser Peter Navarro. (BBG)

South Korea’s export growth slowed sharply in August, with U.S.-bound shipments plunging as President Trump’s tariffs weighed on global trade. Exports rose 1.3% Y/Y vs exp. +3.7% and July's +5.8%. However, Semiconductor exports jumped 27%, driven by demand for high-performance chips used in artificial intelligence, while vehicle shipments gained 9%. (WSJ)

The Czech government is proposing to increase the state budget deficit next year as the fiscally-conservative administration plans to boost spending on defense and a major energy project. (BBG)

Russian oil producers’ profits dived in the first half of the year, driven down by lower crude prices and a stronger ruble. (BBG)

Switzerland’s trade group for gold refiners opposes a relocation of some operations to the US to ease a trade imbalance between the countries and help tariff negotiations, newspaper Neue Zuercher Zeitung reported. (BBG)

Silver Climbs Past $40 as US Rate-Cut Bets Fuel Investor Demand. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Europe is drawing up "pretty precise plans" for a multinational troop deployment to Ukraine as part of post-conflict security guarantees that will have the backing of U.S. capabilities, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told the FT in an interview published Sunday. (FT)

The European Union’s new €150 billion ($175 billion) plan to accelerate investment in the bloc’s defense industry will benefit Poland most, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Sunday. (BBG)

Norway has picked the UK as the supplier of frigates for its navy in a £10bln deal, in what would be the biggest ever investment in the Nordic country’s defense. Norway, who is among the NATO members that border Russia, had also considered France, Germany and the US as a potential strategic partner for the frigates. (BBG)

The EU will discuss options on how to act more swiftly on foreign policy matters, an area in which most decisions need unanimity, which has seen Hungary oppose many actions in favor of Ukraine and against Russia in recent years. (BBG)

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he hasn’t given up hope that a ceasefire can be secured in Ukraine, but he’s “not under any illusions either.” (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Intel said on Friday it amended the CHIPS Act funding deal with the U.S. Department of Commerce to remove earlier project milestones and received about $5.7 billion in cash sooner than planned. (RTRS)

Apple plans to reintroduce finger-print verification when it unveils its 1st foldable iPhone next year, adopting Qualcomm’s in-display fingerprint ID technology as a way to make the device thinner. (UDN via @dnystedt)

ChatGPT parent OpenAI is scouting local partners to set up a data center in India with at least 1 gigawatt capacity, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

Tesla lowered the price for its Model 3 rear-wheel drive version in China by 3.7% to 259,500 yuan ($36,278.99), its website showed on Monday. Tesla launched the new Model 3 variant, its longest-range Tesla model, in China last month. (RTRS)

Spirit Airlines filed for bankruptcy protection on Friday for the second time in a year after a previous reorganization failed to put it on firmer financial footing. (RTRS)

Jefferies among private credit investors exposed to US auto company invoices. (FT)

TSMC will detail its upcoming co-packaged optics (CPO) silicon photonics solution at SEMICON Taiwan (9/10-12), aimed at greatly boosting computing speeds in AI data centers. The chips are expected to be in mass production in 2026. (CTEE via @dnystedt)

SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics shares dropped on Monday after Washington revoked authorisations that allowed them to secure U.S. semiconductor manufacturing equipment for their chip plants in China. (RTRS)

Eric Trump is expected to attend a shareholder meeting of Japanese bitcoin treasury company Metaplanet (3350) in Tokyo on Monday, as the U.S. president's family expands its crypto ventures internationally. (RTRS)

Japan’s top conveyor-belt sushi chain, Sushiro, is leaning on profits from its rapid overseas expansion to take the bite out of surging rice costs at home. (BBG)

Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc has held exploratory talks with advisers over funding options, including an initial public offering, for its small nuclear reactor unit, according to the Financial Times. (FT)

Equinor pledged to support Orsted’s rights issue by subscribing for around $939 million of new shares. (RTRS)

The suspect in the fatal shooting of an employee of Manila Electric Company (Meralco) in a road rage incident in Dasmariñas, Cavite surrendered to authorities on Monday, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said.

In a press conference, DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the suspect “was identified as a resident of his barangay and the barangay captain to his credit immediately went cooperating with the police for the manhunt and the eventual surrender of the suspect.”

The Cavite Police Provincial Police presented the 44 year-old suspect during the press conference.

On August 27, the victim was on his way to his retirement party at the office when he was shot by the suspect in what appeared to be a traffic altercation.
